newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia, Kazakhstan in economic deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia, Kazakhstan in economic deal.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Thursday he had initialled an economic cooperation deal with the resource-rich former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.

Downer said in a statement that the agreement on economic and commercial cooperation was initialled in a meeting with Kazakh First Deputy Prime Minister Akhmetzhan Yesimov, who is accompanying Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev on a state visit to Australia.
The two also signed a bilateral "Memorandum of Understanding on Friendship and Cooperation", Downer said.
Downer said the economic agreement was designed to boost cooperation in sectors such as mining, telecommunications, agriculture and training.
The agreement would also facilitate the entry of Australian companies into the Kazakh market, he added.
Downer said the Central Asian republic of Kazakhstan, which gained independence after the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union, was "a new state with significant investment and development potential".

"It is the ninth largest country in the world in area, and is rich in natural resources such as precious metal and oil," he added. Bilateral trade in 1995/96 was valued at A$18.5 million.
